title: Volleyball
description: Test your knowledge of spikes, sets, and serves!

questions.question: How many players from one team are on the court during indoor volleyball?
questions.explanation: Indoor volleyball teams field 6 players: 3 in the front row and 3 in the back row.

questions.question: How many points are typically needed to win a set in indoor volleyball?
questions.explanation: Sets are played to 25 points, win by 2 (except the deciding 5th set, played to 15).

questions.question: A team is allowed three contacts before sending the ball over the net.
questions.explanation: Typically: a bump (pass), set, then spike. A block does not count as one of the three.

questions.question: What is the defensive specialist position called who wears a different colored jersey?
questions.explanation: The libero is a back-row defensive specialist who wears a contrasting jersey.

questions.question: Which country has won the most Olympic gold medals in men's indoor volleyball?
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union/Russia leads men's Olympic volleyball with the most golds historically.

questions.question: Beach volleyball is played with two players per team.
questions.explanation: Standard beach volleyball is 2v2, with no substitutions during a match.

questions.question: What is a 'kill' in volleyball?

options.text: A serve that no one returns
An attack that directly results in a point

questions.explanation: A kill is an attack hit that the opponent cannot return, resulting in a point or side-out.

questions.question: How high is the net for men's indoor volleyball?
questions.explanation: The men's net is set at 2.43 meters; the women's net is 2.24 meters.

questions.question: What is it called when a serve lands in the opponent's court untouched?
questions.explanation: An ace is a serve that scores directly without the opposing team returning it.

questions.question: Players must rotate clockwise after winning a side-out.
questions.explanation: Rotation is clockwise, but it occurs after the receiving team wins the rally to serve.
